comment: Documented exceptions for the production npm-audit release gate (scripts/audit-gate.cjs). Two shapes: (1) per-GHSA {id,...} allowlists ONE advisory; (2) location-scoped {package, locationContains,...} allowlists ANY advisory for `package` whose EVERY affected install path contains `locationContains` — for a transitive pinned inside an upstream npm-shrinkwrap.json (unfixable downstream), so each new disclosure for that frozen copy need not be re-listed. The 'every node in scope' rule keeps location-scoping precise: it fires only when no remediable copy is affected. Any advisory NOT matched (per-id or location) still fails the gate at moderate+. Every entry must carry reason, clearsWhen, reviewed. Re-verify at every release; the gate warns on stale entries.

exceptions.reason: adm-zip 0.5.9-0.6.0 follows symbolic links at the extraction destination (CVE-2026-76845), so an archive whose path component at the destination is a pre-existing symlink pointing outside the root gets written through it. Unfixable here, in BOTH directions: first_patched_version on the advisory is null and adm-zip 0.6.0 (published 2026-07-10) is the newest release ever published, so no fixed version exists to bump or npm-override to; and the apparent alternative of overriding DOWN below the vulnerable range (0.5.8) reintroduces GHSA-xcpc-8h2w-3j85 (CVE-2026-39244, HIGH, affected <0.6.0, patched exactly in 0.6.0) — a strictly worse trade — besides being outside both parents' declared ranges (onnxruntime-node ^0.5.16, camoufox-js ^0.6.0; onnxruntime-node@1.29.0, the latest upstream, still requires ^0.6.0). The vulnerable copy enters the production tree as a single deduped node_modules/adm-zip that is a direct dependency of both onnxruntime-node (via @huggingface/transformers, used in this package only for text embeddings) and camoufox-js. Exposure is low but not zero, and the two call sites differ: camoufox-js downloads camoufox-*.zip from the trusted daijro/camoufox GitHub releases and extracts into the per-user cache dir (a compromised release would already mean executing a hostile browser binary, so the symlink bug adds nothing); onnxruntime-node's postinstall downloads the onnxruntime NuGet zip over HTTPS with no checksum and extracts it via extractEntryTo into os.tmpdir()/onnxruntime-node-pkgs_<Date.now()> — a predictable-name directory in the shared world-writable temp dir — so a LOCAL attacker racing the install can pre-plant destination symlinks and overwrite files as the installing user (CWE-59 is destination-side, so 'trusted archive' alone does not close the vector; it requires local access plus a timing race during npm install, which keeps it below the blocking bar in this repo's threat model).
exceptions.clearsWhen: adm-zip publishes a release outside the vulnerable range >=0.5.9 <=0.6.0 AND the pinning parents (onnxruntime-node, camoufox-js) resolve to it (add a temporary override if a parent lags). An upstream fix is already in progress: cthackers/adm-zip PR #575 (open since 2026-09-01, mergeable, rewrites util/utils.js with symlink regression tests) — watch for its merge and the following release. Remove this entry at that point and re-run the gate.
